'''Mariusz Wodzicki''' (<small>Polish</small>: {{IPAc-pl|'|m|a|r|j|u|sz|-|w|o|'|dź|i|c|k|J|i}}; born 1956) is a Polish [[mathematician]] and professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], whose works primarily focus on [[analysis]], algebraic [[K-theory]], [[noncommutative geometry]], and [[algebraic geometry]].

==Life and career==
Wodzicki was born in [[Bytom]], [[Poland]] in 1956. He received a [[Master of Science|MSc]] from [[Moscow State University]] in 1980,<ref name="IAS">{{cite web|url=https://library.ias.edu/files/pdfs/ar/reportforacademi1987inst.pdf|title=Annual Report 1986/1987|publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]]|location=[[Princeton, New Jersey]]|page=41|access-date=July 8, 2020}}</ref> and he completed his doctoral degree in 1984 at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] in [[Moscow]] under the advisement of [[Yuri Manin]] (Spectral Asymmetry and Zeta-Functions).<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=32914}}</ref> 

In 1985–1986 he was a research assistant at the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford]], after which he became an assistant professor at the Mathematical Institute of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="IAS"/> He is currently a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/mariusz-wodzicki| title=Homepage of Mariusz Wodzicki|publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]]}}</ref>

In 1992, Wodzicki was an invited speaker of the [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in [[Paris]] (Algebraic K-theory and functional analysis). In 1994, he was an invited speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zürich]] (The algebra of functional analysis).<ref>Not printed in the proceedings</ref>
